sources.title: Accessing files from the macOS App Sandbox
sources.version_commit: Living Apple Developer documentation; search-index snapshot crawled approximately 2026-07.
sources.locator: Sections “Persist file access with security-scoped URL bookmarks” and “Access files related to documents with document-relative bookmarks.”
sources.observed_operation: Opened and read indexed primary documentation; direct page indicates JavaScript is required.
sources.governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: Security-scoped bookmarks permit later access after app relaunch but require resolving, stale-bookmark refresh, start/stop access calls, and appropriate sandbox entitlements. Document-relative bookmarks can be stored in the owning project document and resolved when the app can access that project.
sources.applicability: Supports the draft’s macOS sandbox access adapter and project-scoped permission idea; does not provide cross-platform file identity or recovery.

sources.title: URLResourceKey.documentIdentifierKey
sources.version_commit: Living Apple Foundation API documentation; indexed snapshot crawled approximately 2026-09.
sources.observed_operation: Searched Apple’s official docs; read returned indexed primary-document text. A direct open required JavaScript.
sources.governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: Kernel-assigned document identifier follows a move on one volume, persists across restarts, is not transferred by copy, is unique only within one volume, and is unsupported on some volumes; safe-save may preserve it.
sources.applicability: Supports an optional macOS same-volume candidate-comparison hint, not a path resolver or universal identity. Minimum OS/filesystem support remains unresolved.

sources.title: FILE_ID_INFO structure (winbase.h)
sources.observed_operation: Opened and read the Microsoft Learn API page.
sources.governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: GetFileInformationByHandleEx returns a volume serial number and 128-bit file ID; comparing both open-handle values identifies the same file on a single computer.
sources.applicability: Useful Windows live comparison hint; not a portable project locator or cross-computer identity.

sources.title: ReadDirectoryChangesW function
sources.locator: bWatchSubtree parameter and Remarks on zero-byte results, buffer overflow, ERROR_NOTIFY_ENUM_DIR, and unsupported redirectors/filesystems.
sources.observed_operation: Opened and read the Microsoft Learn API page, especially lines 61–62 and 113–130.
sources.governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: Subtree watching is caller-selected. On overflow the entire notification buffer is discarded; a zero-byte result or ERROR_NOTIFY_ENUM_DIR requires re-enumeration. Some network redirectors/filesystems do not support the operation.
sources.applicability: Supports watcher use as a best-effort refresh signal only, followed by reconciliation; not a lossless durable path-tracking system.

sources.title: inotify(7) — Linux manual page
sources.version_commit: Linux man-pages living documentation; page version not pinned in the fetched/indexed result.
sources.locator: DESCRIPTION, rename handling, limitations and caveats.
sources.observed_operation: Direct page fetch timed out; searched the primary Linux manual and inspected its indexed page text for watch and event semantics.
sources.governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: Indexed primary text identifies directory watches, event-queue lifecycle, and the need for robust handling of monitoring races. The carried source map records nonrecursive watches, racy rename pairing, overflow, remote-filesystem omissions, and watch removal on unmount.
sources.applicability: Supports only a best-effort Linux status hint. Specific current kernel/filesystem behavior should be verified when implementing a watcher.

sources.title: Zotero attachments.js
sources.version_commit: Zotero release tag 6.0.20; Git commit SHA not captured by the carried map.
sources.observed_operation: Opened the tagged GitHub source and inspected the code around the cited methods; did not execute code.
sources.governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: linkFromFile creates a LINK_MODE_LINKED_FILE record. The relative-path method rejects missing/absolute paths, prefixes the configured base placeholder, stores the linked record, and processes/indexes the file only when the base resolves and the target exists.
sources.applicability: Concrete version-pinned implementation precedent for explicit linked-file records and base-relative paths. Does not establish portable identity or that Zotero’s behavior should be copied wholesale.

sources.title: Zotero 6.0 Version History
sources.locator: 6.0.16 linked-file auto-location entry and 6.0.20 macOS/Linux-to-Windows relink fix.
sources.observed_operation: Opened the official version-history page and inspected the 6.0.16 and 6.0.20 release sections.
sources.governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: 6.0.16 offered to locate missing files under the configured Linked Attachment Base Directory and relink one file or same-base-path files. 6.0.20 fixed an automatic relinking problem when moving from macOS/Linux to Windows.
sources.applicability: Shipped precedent for bounded search and a real cross-platform regression; does not validate this notebook’s proposed matching algorithm.

sources.title: SQLite Transaction
sources.version_commit: Living SQLite documentation; version not pinned.
sources.locator: Sections 2.1 and 2.2, especially simultaneous readers/writer and SQLITE_BUSY behavior.
sources.observed_operation: Opened and inspected the official SQLite transaction documentation.
sources.governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: SQLite permits simultaneous read transactions but only one simultaneous write transaction; write upgrades can fail SQLITE_BUSY, and readers may continue seeing a historic snapshot until their transaction ends.
sources.applicability: Supports SQLite as a conditional storage example. Application revision checks and same-record conflict UX remain product responsibilities.

sources.title: Distributed Link Tracking and Object Identifiers
sources.observed_operation: Opened the Microsoft Learn API overview and inspected its limitation section.
sources.governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: Tracking is limited to NTFS 3.0+; FAT moves lose tracking; links to files on removable media are not maintained; a newly connected NTFS volume may not be recognized until reboot.
sources.applicability: Confirms DLT is not a required or sufficient cross-platform/removable-drive core.

sources.title: File System Events Programming Guide: Using the File System Events API
sources.version_commit: Apple archived guide, updated 2012-12-13; original API documentation release/version not otherwise pinned.
sources.locator: Handling Events and Building a Directory Hierarchy Snapshot, lines 101–168.
sources.observed_operation: Opened the Apple archive and read event coalescing, dropped-event, root-change, and rescan requirements.
sources.governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: Events may coalesce; dropped kernel/user events require a full scan; root moves/renames can invalidate watched paths; for accurate snapshots, start monitoring before scanning and rescan modified subdirectories.
sources.applicability: Supports a conservative optional macOS refresh watcher. Archived age warrants validation against the selected current SDK/OS if implementation proceeds.
